text:
alex: Heads-up: ran the streaming chat vs non-streaming completions perf sweep on rtx-pool-7, results are...surprising. Need opinions on kernel routing + mb sizing tradeoffs.

priya: thanks, can you paste the key numbers? p95/p99 and throughput per-GPU?

alex: short version: streaming chat (streaming=true) with mb_size=4 gives lower median but p99 balloons vs mb_size=1. Non-streaming completions scale well up to mb_size=12 for throughput but p95 gets worse for short prompts.

josh: that matches intuition — streaming hurts when there's tail work from last-token flushes and many small KV hits. Did you check KV cache hit rate?

alex: yes. KV hit rate for chat seqs was ~78% after warmup, but the effective kernel work per request still higher because of more frequent small batches and kernel switches. Profile snippet: 
```
Profile summary (per-GPU):
workload: streaming_chat / 1.6k reqs
avg latency: 62 ms
p95 latency: 210 ms
p99 latency: 480 ms
throughput: 1.1k tok/s
kernel time breakdown: flash_attn 52%, fallback_gemm 34%, memcpy/overhead 14%
kv cache hits: 78% (warm), misses dominated by new conversations
```

maya: do we see kernel churn? i.e., flash_attn often falling back for tails?

alex: yes, especially at mb_size>8 when sequence lengths vary — the scheduler picks flash_attn for shorter lanes but falls back when combined sequence length > threshold. That fallback spike aligns with p99 spikes.

priya: what about non-streaming completions numbers?

alex: non-streaming completions (batched sync responses) with mb_size=12: 
```
avg: 88 ms
p95: 160 ms
p99: 260 ms
throughput: 2.6k tok/s
kernel mix: triton_fused 68%, fallback 22%, overhead 10%
```

josh: interesting — completions get better kernel hit rates at larger mb because sequences are more homogeneous. Streaming chat has high variance in live token production.

infra-bot: deploy note: the experiment used kernel build v2026-02, cached kernels cleared before run.

maya: proposed operational rules: route streaming chat to a small-static mb policy (1-4) + strict p95 SLO; route non-streaming completions to larger mb (8-16) with throughput-first SLO. Thoughts on exact thresholds?

priya: +1. Also suggest kernel routing heuristic: prefer flash_attn only if avg_seq_len_in_batch < 512 and batch_size>=2; else prefer triton_fused. That would reduce fallback spikes.

alex: tried a quick rule in runtime config: 
```
kernel_policy:
  - if avg_len < 512 and batch >= 2: prefer flash_attn
  - else: prefer triton_fused
mb_policy:
  streaming_chat: target_mb: 2, max_mb: 4, p95_target_ms: 150
  completions: target_mb: 10, max_mb: 16, p95_target_ms: 250
kv_cache:
  prefetch: true
  prewarm_prefixes: true
```

josh: did that reduce p99 spikes on the next run?

alex: partially. p95 for streaming dropped to 145ms, p99 still had occasional 420-500ms spikes when KV misses + fallback coincided. We need better isolation for tail work.

maya: could we use tail-shed: detect MBs with >X long lanes and move them to a separate 'tail' queue processed with different kernel/time quota?

priya: yes — we can mark batches with high seq variance and route them to a lower-priority pool with smaller mb and stricter per-request CPU/GPU quotas. That adds throughput cost but protects SLO.

eva: quick note from evals: user-facing quality for streaming chat dropped slightly when we forced mb_size=1 (due to less context for cache aggregation), but not enough to matter for most apps. Worth balancing.

josh: what about adaptive mb that reacts to recent p95? e.g., increase mb for completions if p95 below threshold, decrease for streaming when queue latency trending up.

alex: we have that prototype. It oscillates under bursty traffic. Need hysteresis and a KV-aware signal (prefetch hit rate) to avoid thrashing.

maya: next action items:
- alex: run targeted runs with kernel_policy rule + tail-queue for streaming (2h, peak traffic) by EOD
- priya: add a runtime metric: batch_seq_variance and last-kv-hit-rate for routing decisions
- josh: sketch tail-queue design and cost estimates (throughput loss vs p99 reduction)
- eva: run quality-sensitivity test for mb=1..4 on representative prompts

alex: thanks — I'll post the raw traces (perf traces + kernel profiler) in the thread after the run. If we converge, we'll make a default: streaming->small-static-mb + tail-queue; completions->large-dynamic-mb with kernel preferring fused kernels.

priya: sounds good. one more: include an experiment to precompile smaller-kernel-specializations for typical streaming lengths (128/256) to reduce fallback overhead.

infra-bot: FYI: experiment cluster rtx-pool-7 will be reclaimed at 2026-07-12T03:00Z unless extended.

alex: noted. will prioritize. :thumbsup:
